meta.methodology: Read framework.md, torah_159_packages.json, all reference===159 edges from torahData.js (5 bechina edges, 1 eitza edge), and the full source text torah_159.txt (16 lines). Every bechina-language statement in the source text was identified: explicit language בְּחִינַת, הַיְנוּ, הוּא X, כֵּן הוּא. Only genuine bechina declarations (not causal/eitza, not mere simile, not narrative description) were treated as gap candidates. Each candidate was checked against the dataset to determine whether the concept and edge appear in reference===159 data.

concepts_examined_and_excluded.reason: Lines 6 and 13 mention gardinei nimusin — the destructive nighttime forces described in the Zohar (Meketz 203b) — as the agents that strike and disperse Torah that cannot ascend. Line 13 describes them using 'בְּחִינַת': 'הַיְנוּ בְּחִינַת הַגַּרְדִּינֵי נִימוּסִין'. However, this is a cross-reference identification (הַיְנוּ = the same thing mentioned above), not a new bechina equation. The gardinei nimusin are a named entity from Zohar cited as the mechanism of Torah's dispersion — they are narrative actors in the eitza chain (they strike the Torah and cause it to fall/scatter), not bechina-equivalent concepts to other nodes in this Torah. Their role is causal (eitza), not parallel-nature. Excluded as eitza agent.

Lines 6 and 13 describe night (לַיְלָה) as when the gardinei nimusin emerge and strike Torah that cannot ascend. Night is a narrative/temporal setting in the teaching, not declared a bechina of any concept. The Rebbe does not say 'night is a bechina of X' — it is used literally as the time when the gardinei nimusin are active. Excluded as a narrative element, not a bechina concept.

Lines 7 and 13 describe how dispersed Torah spreads through the air (בָּאֲוִיר) and people absorb it from the air. Air is the medium/space through which dispersed Torah travels — a physical setting in the metaphysical narrative, not declared a bechina of any spiritual concept. No בְּחִינַת language is used for it. Excluded.

Lines 14-16 describe physical dew as a mashal (analogy) with two forces: life-giving and death-dealing. The Rebbe says: 'כֵּן נַעֲשֶׂה מֵהַתּוֹרוֹת... שֶׁהֵם מַמָּשׁ בִּבְחִינַת הַטַּל הַגַּשְׁמִי'. This uses 'בְּחִינַת הַטַּל הַגַּשְׁמִי' — but this means the Torah's mechanism IS LIKE physical dew, comparing the spiritual reality to the physical analog. This is analogical/illustrative language confirming the parallel, not a bechina equation between spiritual Torah dew and physical dew as separate concepts. Physical dew serves as the mashal (parable) that illuminates the nimshal (the Torah's main point). It is not a bechina-concept node in its own right. Excluded.

This is a description of WHERE the spiritual abundance goes — the upper worlds and angels — not a bechina-equivalent concept to שפע רוחניות or ימין. The Rebbe says: 'שֶׁזֹּאת הַשֶּׁפַע הִיא לְעוֹלָם שֶׁכֻּלּוֹ אָרֹךְ' — this shefa is FOR that world, not IS that world. Excluded as destination/description, not a bechina equivalence.

Line 8: when a person absorbs Torah from multiple people, 'נַעֲשֶׂה אֶצְלוֹ צֵרוּפִין חֲדָשִׁים' (new letter-combinations form within him), enabling חִדּוּשִׁין. The tzeirufim are a mechanism that PRODUCES chiddushim (eitza), not a bechina-parallel to chiddushim. The Rebbe explains the mechanism causally: 'כִּי כְּשֶׁמְּקַבֵּל מִכַּמָּה תּוֹרוֹת... נַעֲשֶׂה... צֵרוּפִין חֲדָשִׁים, וְיוּכַל לְהַשִּׂיג... חִדּוּשִׁין' — absorbing many Torahs CREATES new combinations which ENABLE insights. This is a causal chain (eitza), not a bechina parallel-nature equation. Excluded.
